docs.title: MSF Laravel Monorepo
docs.text: This repository is the monorepo for the MSF Laravel package ecosystem. It groups reusable library packages for core utilities, auth, users, GraphQL, and other business domains into a single workspace that can be installed and validated as a coherent platform.

docs.title: What is in this repo
docs.text:
The monorepo includes packages such as:

  • msflib/core for shared kernel primitives and utilities
  • msflib/auth for authentication and authorization features
  • msflib/user for user-specific domain logic and scaffolding
  • msflib/graphql for GraphQL integration and Lighthouse setup
  • msflib/config, msflib/common, msflib/inventory, msflib/sales, msflib/notify, and related packages for domain-specific functionality
  • testsite as a consumer app used to validate package installation via the private registry

docs.title: Repository structure
docs.text:
laravel/
├── packages/
│   ├── msflib-core/
│   ├── msflib-auth/
│   ├── msflib-user/
│   ├── msflib-graphql/
│   ├── msflib-config/
│   ├── msflib-common/
│   ├── msflib-inventory/
│   ├── msflib-sales/
│   ├── msflib-notify/
│   ├── msflib-ledger/
│   ├── msflib-accounting/
│   └── ...
├── testsite/
├── README.md
├── composer.json
├── satis.json
├── mkdocs.yml
└── .github/

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• PHP 8.2+
  • Composer
  • Laravel-compatible local environment
  • Optional: access to the private registry or Satis bucket for downstream install tests

docs.title: Bootstrapping the monorepo
docs.text:
From the repo root:

cd laravel
composer install

For package-level validation:

for file in packages/*/composer.json; do
  composer validate --working-dir="$(dirname "$file")" --no-check-publish --no-check-lock
done

docs.title: Monorepo validation
docs.text:
The project provides monorepo validation tooling:

composer monorepo:validate

This is the main way to validate the workspace structure and package relationships before a release or change is merged.

docs.title: Composer package pattern
docs.text:
The root repository config declares path repositories for all packages under packages/*. This allows local package development without publishing every package to Packagist or a private registry first.

"repositories": [
  {
    "type": "path",
    "url": "packages/*",
    "options": {
      "symlink": true
    }
  }
]

This pattern is how local monorepo work is wired together before pushing to a branch or release channel.

docs.title: Consumer app installation model
docs.text:
This monorepo is designed to be consumed from downstream Laravel apps via Composer artifacts and a private registry mirror, not only through direct path repositories.

{
  "repositories": [
    {
      "type": "artifact",
      "url": ".msflib-registry/dist"
    }
  ],
  "require": {
    "msflib/user": "dev-dev"
  }
}

A downstream app mirrors the registry channel and then installs the package normally. This is the pattern documented in the project README and used by testsite.

docs.title: Package map
docs.text:
• Core — foundational utilities and framework-agnostic primitives
  • Auth — authentication service provider and permissions integration
  • User — user domain and user service package
  • GraphQL — Lighthouse and GraphQL package layer
  • Registry — Satis, artifact mirroring, and release channels
  • Summary — docs index

docs.title: Important operational notes
docs.text:
• package releases are managed through the monorepo and private registry workflow
  • packages are released as versioned artifacts and then mirrored into downstream app installs
  • the root workspace uses service providers from package providers to register Laravel features at runtime

docs.title: Typical local usage
docs.text:
composer install
php artisan test

The exact commands depend on the package or app under test, but the monorepo workflow is intentionally organized around package-level validation and downstream consumer verification.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text: The msflib/auth package provides authentication and authorization functionality for Laravel apps using the MSF package ecosystem.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
This package integrates:

  • JWT authentication via php-open-source-saver/jwt-auth
  • permission handling with spatie/laravel-permission
  • GraphQL-related auth support through msflib/graphql
  • user integration through msflib/user

docs.title: Dependency pattern
docs.text:
{
  "require": {
    "php": "^8.2",
    "msflib/graphql": "dev-dev",
    "msflib/user": "dev-dev",
    "php-open-source-saver/jwt-auth": "^2.0",
    "spatie/laravel-permission": "^6.0"
  }
}

docs.title: Service provider registration
docs.text:
'providers' => [
    MsfLib\Auth\MsfAuthServiceProvider::class,
],

This is how the package is normally discovered in a Laravel app.

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
use MsfLib\Auth\Services\AuthService;

$token = app(AuthService::class)->issueToken($user);

The package is intended to provide the authentication layer behind business-specific user, session, and access logic.

docs.title: Considerations
docs.text:
• keep auth concerns separated from business logic packages where possible
  • rely on Laravel service provider discovery for integration
  • prefer package-specific configuration for JWT and permissions rather than coupling to app code

docs.title: Core
docs.text: The msflib/core package is the shared kernel for the broader Laravel monorepo. It contains foundational cross-cutting code and should remain framework-agnostic in the sense that it is not meant to absorb package-specific business logic from the higher-level domain packages.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
This package is responsible for:

  • shared base infrastructure and conventions
  • common exceptions and primitives
  • framework-agnostic utilities and patterns
  • base service registration for downstream packages

docs.title: Dependency pattern
docs.text:
{
  "require": {
    "php": "^8.2"
  }
}

The package is intentionally lightweight and is the foundation for packages such as msflib/auth, msflib/user, and msflib/graphql.

docs.title: Service provider integration
docs.text:
public function register(): void
{
    $this->app->singleton('msflib.core', function () {
        return new \Msflib\Core\CoreManager();
    });
}

This package is registered through its Laravel service provider and then used by sibling packages that layer on domain-specific logic.

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
use MsfLib\Core\Support\Str;

$value = Str::slug('My Example Value');

The exact implementation should follow the actual classes in the package, but the intent is that msflib/core remains the reusable, low-level toolkit for the rest of the monorepo.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• keep it generic and reusable
  • avoid coupling it to a specific business domain
  • expose helpers that multiple package types can share without duplication
  • prefer package-level service providers for domain setup

docs.title: GraphQL
docs.text: The msflib/graphql package provides the GraphQL integration layer for the Laravel monorepo. It is built around the Lighthouse ecosystem and is intended to provide a shared GraphQL foundation for downstream packages.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
This package provides:

  • GraphQL schema integration
  • Lighthouse configuration support
  • shared platform primitives for GraphQL-facing packages
  • integration with msflib/core and downstream domain packages

docs.title: Dependency pattern
docs.text:
{
  "require": {
    "php": "^8.2",
    "mll-lab/graphql-php-scalars": "^6.0",
    "msflib/core": "dev-dev",
    "nuwave/lighthouse": "^6.29"
  }
}

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
use Nuwave\Lighthouse\Schema\SourceSchemaFinder;

return [
    'schema' => [
        'default' => 'default',
    ],
];

The package is intended to be the GraphQL service layer that other packages can build on without duplicating configuration or schema bootstrap code.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• keep GraphQL concerns centralized in this package
  • use package-level service providers for registration
  • make downstream package integration consistent rather than custom per package

docs.title: Registry
docs.text: The Laravel monorepo publishes package artifacts through a private Composer registry workflow based on Satis and DigitalOcean Spaces. This is a core part of how downstream apps consume the packages without depending on direct local path configuration in production.

docs.title: Why this exists
docs.text:
The monorepo is not just a local workspace. It is designed to produce installable packages for downstream Laravel applications. The registry layer makes that possible by:

  • staging package artifacts for each branch or release
  • generating provider metadata from the monorepo
  • mirroring the registry into a cache directory for consumer apps
  • supporting both dev and main channels

docs.title: Relevant configuration
docs.text:
• root composer.json
  • satis.json
  • .github/workflows/satis-publish.yml
  • .github/workflows/satis-release.yml

docs.title: Downstream consumer flow
docs.text:
A downstream app mirrors the registry to a local folder before installing dependencies:

{
  "repositories": [
    {
      "type": "artifact",
      "url": ".msflib-registry/dist"
    }
  ],
  "require": {
    "msflib/user": "dev-dev"
  }
}

The pre-install-cmd and pre-update-cmd hooks can then run the registry mirror script automatically before Composer resolves dependencies.

docs.title: Channel model
docs.text:
The project uses separate channels for development and production-oriented releases:

  • dev for branch-based package publishing
  • main for tagged release publishing

This avoids collisions between floating development package versions and stable release versions.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
composer monorepo:validate
composer monorepo:release:dry-run

These are the main local commands for validating package metadata and release readiness before publishing.

docs.title: User
docs.text: The msflib/user package contains the user-oriented domain layer and associated Laravel integrations for the monorepo.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
This package focuses on:

  • user models and default user behavior
  • Laravel service provider registration
  • relationship and permission integration with downstream packages
  • domain services built on top of msflib/core

docs.title: Dependency pattern
docs.text:
{
  "require": {
    "php": "^8.2",
    "laravel/framework": "^10.0",
    "msflib/core": "dev-dev",
    "msflib/graphql": "dev-dev",
    "spatie/laravel-permission": "^6.0"
  }
}

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
use MsfLib\User\Models\User;

$user = User::query()->first();

The package is intended to centralize the user domain rather than scatter that logic across unrelated packages in the monorepo.

docs.title: Notes for consumers
docs.text:
• the package is meant to be consumed as a reusable library from a Laravel app
  • the service provider is the integration point for app bootstrapping
  • user-related GraphQL and permission features are layered on top of the package rather than stored in the app itself
